feature: Landing screen: new project / import file

feature: Header: Home button, version label (opens changelog)

feature: Header: New / Save / Load project buttons

what: Camera button calls `handleSnapshot`

notes: Unverified what the snapshot outputs (image vs state copy). Only the handler name was seen

what: Sun/moon button switches dark and light
home: Design system light and dark themes, artboard 1; Phase 2
notes: Same control appears in header, settings and phone menu. Keep one
recWhy: Theme is a setting in the design system; a header shortcut is optional.

what: Opens settings on the accessibility tab
notes: Duplicate entry point

what: Opens Help center

recWhy: One help entry that reopens the first-run guide and help pages.

feature: Header: Select tool vs Zone tool switch

notes: Linking and drawing modes must show a banner (artboard 3 wire-mode banner)
recWhy: Select and zone tools are needed in the editor; the mode banner and cancel rule apply. Unverified.

notes: Zones are physical enclosures. Phase 5 panel layout may reuse them, or not. Undecided
recWhy: Zones are drawn in Phase 2, so the layers pane (hide, lock, rename, centre) ships with them; deferring leaves zones unmanageable. Unverified.

what: Gear opens simulation settings tab

notes: Needs engine support for LOTO, tempGround, faults, leakage. Phase 3 needs the switching-order logic

what: Zoom in, zoom out, fit all, centre (0,0)
notes: Not shown on phones

what: Toggle grid, snap to grid, show zones, show axes

what: Collapsible left panel; switches content by mode; Edit-mode footer button for load balance report

notes: Replaces separate Edit/Sim sidebar pairs

what: Collapsible right panel; Edit mode shows library, Sim mode shows details
notes: Same as UI-020
recWhy: Same finding as UI-020: no mode-dependent sidebar swapping; one collapsible persistent panel layout.

what: Searchable grid of component cards in 10 groups (energy sources, solar, generation, transformation, switching, busbar, loads, control, graphics, general); flat/grouped toggle; drag or click to add; info button
home: Library panel, artboard 1; library shrinks to ~20-24 types; Phase 2 (core 8 first, rest Phase 4)
notes: Card shows a 3-letter code, not a symbol. Symbols layer is a separate package
recWhy: Library is redesigned around the 20-24 types; the first eight components ship in Phase 2 and the rest in Phase 4. Unverified.

what: Info (i) on a card opens spec: functional description, logic and behaviour, operating states, engineering parameters
notes: Text is hard-coded per type in code. Make it catalog data and translatable

what: Tooltip with component summary on hover
recWhy: A hover summary is a short form of the info panel; one source for both.

what: Shows count; says move, rotate (R) and delete (Del) work on the group
recWhy: Multi-selection feedback is useful; show count and group actions in the inspector.

what: Label text, show/hide, label position, routing mode (orthogonal/direct), text colour, background colour, font size, fixed-size label
home: Inspector appearance group; compound wire, artboard 5; Phase 2
notes: Design finding: colour pickers sat above engineering data. Appearance goes last
recWhy: Wire label and routing options move into the compound-wire inspector with appearance last. Unverified.

what: Cable model, cross-section, length, parallel cores, material properties (conductor, insulation, resistivity), R and X per phase

notes: Blue Grid silently defaulted to N2XY 150 mm2 100 m. Flow Engine must show required fields or a diagnostic
recWhy: Compound-wire inspector is right; required fields or a diagnostic replace Blue Grid's silent N2XY 150 mm2 100 m default.

what: Modal: working current, connected circuit, insulation (90C/70C), installation method (31 methods per Israeli electricity law), ambient/soil temperature, thermal resistance, adjacent circuits, parallel cables; outputs corrected current Iz, required In, cable cross-section, actual capacity; button "Apply to wire"
home: Cable sizing in engine and standards profile; no mockup yet; calculator surface Phase 3
notes: Hard-coded to Israeli law. Brief: must become a swappable standards profile. Engine cable-sizing is a Phase 1+ gate
recWhy: Same feature as CH-011: cable sizing is a Phase 1 engine gate under the standards profile; this modal surface is Phase 2 in the inspector.

what: Zone name, background colour, title position (9-grid), width, height, delete
home: Annotation layer; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: See UI-015
recWhy: Zone name, colour, size and title position are basic properties of zones drawn in Phase 2 and used for location text. Unverified.

what: "Select a component, wire or zone" message
recWhy: Empty-selection hint is trivial and useful in the inspector. Unverified.

what: Label visible, position, text and background colour, sticky size; per-field "show on diagram" eye toggle
home: Schema-driven forms (basic, rating, protection, appearance), artboard 1; Phase 2
notes: Per-field "show on component" toggles: keep as appearance setting
recWhy: Appearance group of the schema-driven form; label and colours stay per element.

what: Monitor on/off, monitor label, parent (drag), diversity factor
home: Load aggregation view; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Maps to load aggregation with traceable totals
recWhy: Monitoring groups with a diversity factor map to load aggregation, a Phase 4 view over the full calculation.

what: Voltage type, frequency, power, source impedance %, short-circuit MVA (grid); GEN adds fuel consumption, capacity, current fuel
home: Inspector schema forms; artboard 1; Phase 2 (grid, gen core set)
notes: Fuel fields belong to FUEL_TANK (Phase 4)
recWhy: Schema-driven source forms replace hand-written ones; fuel fields move to the fuel tank in phase 4.

feature: Properties: switching devices (breaker, disconnector, earth switch, load breaker, fuse)
what: Voltage rating, current rating, interrupting capacity (breaker)
home: Single switch with capability set; artboard 1; Phase 2
notes: Breaking capacity must be compared with fault current (design finding)
recWhy: One switch type with a capability set drives which rating fields show.

what: L setting/delay, S setting/delay, I setting, G setting; button to open time-current curve
home: Protection curves and selectivity; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Settings kept as protection profile, not a type
recWhy: Protection profile fields need the curve engine, which is Phase 4.

what: Modal chart of L, S, I, G curves for a breaker; Save as image
home: Protection curves and selectivity; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Blue Grid draws curves from settings only. No selectivity verdict seen in this file
recWhy: Time-current curves belong with selectivity in Phase 4; image export is a separate owner choice.

what: Power, primary, secondary, %Z, no-load loss, full-load loss, connection group, phase shift
notes: Design: vector group regex-parsed, impedance side bug. Needs reference cases

what: Voltage type, power, leakage current, voltage rating; EV charger extras
home: Merged load with mode (kVA or A) and symbol; artboard 1; Phase 2 (EV Phase 4)
notes: LOAD, CURRENT_LOAD, LIGHT, HORN merge
recWhy: Merged load form, with the EV charger extras in Phase 4.

feature: Properties: converters, UPS, battery, other types
what: Inverter/VFD/DCDC/rectifier input and output type, frequencies; UPS power, backup time, recharge factor, initial charge; RCD, battery bank, fuel tank, busbar, pole, connector, current stabilizer (CCR) input voltage, max power, target current, efficiency
home: Remaining components and series loops; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Type merges per concepts brief triage (converter, UPS, DC busbar)
recWhy: These types arrive in Phase 4 with the merged converter and battery model.

feature: Properties: control logic (interlock, synchronizer, ATS, ATS controller)
what: Pick linked components, generator, main/secondary breaker, logic type
home: One control-logic layer; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Brief: ATS and ATS_CONTROLLER duplicate. Links bound by label text must become ID bindings
recWhy: Control logic is one Phase 4 layer, with links bound by ID instead of label text. Unverified.

what: Fill, outline colour, line width, corner radius, text content, arrow head size, double arrow
home: Annotation layer outside electrical model; no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: Annotation style properties belong with the Phase 2 annotation layer (CH-019, CH-020); splitting them into Phase 4 leaves annotations unstyled. Unverified.

what: Load a project into a subsystem, export contents to file, add/remove/rename ports with connector and grid position
home: Subsystem redesign (loose string links); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Port label match ties connector to subsystem. Must bind by ID
recWhy: Subsystem ports and loading become a Phase 4 view over the full calculation, bound by ID not label. Unverified.

feature: Sim right panel: selected item header and status
what: Name, type, "connected and live / disconnected / system fault" badge, error text
home: Results with calculation trace and problems panel; artboard 4; Phase 1 (console, artboard 2) then 2
notes: Error text becomes a coded diagnostic with entity IDs
recWhy: Phase 1 has no editor, so the selected-item results panel with coded diagnostics ships with the editor; the console covers phase 1.

what: Voltage, current, frequency, supply type
home: Results with trace, artboards 2 and 4; Phase 1/2
notes: Add trace and assumed-value flag
recWhy: Voltage, current and frequency appear first in the Phase 1 console, then on the editor.

what: Instant/average/max load meters, I and P average/max, measured duration, reset measurement
home: Load analysis view; no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: Live monitoring meters over a rehearsal do not fit a calculation tool. Static load aggregation (UI-032, SIM-046) covers design loading. Your call.

what: L1, L2, L3 voltage, current and phase angle
home: Results, balanced-model estimate label; artboard 4; Phase 1/2
notes: Design: unbalanced results are labelled estimates. Colours conflict with red=fault; use identity tokens
recWhy: Per-phase values come from the balanced model and must carry an estimate label.

feature: Sim panel: loss and voltage-drop analysis
what: Wire voltage drop, thermal power loss, impedance triangle (R, X, Z)
notes: Two voltage-drop solvers existed; keep one
recWhy: Voltage drop, loss and impedance come from the single engine in Phase 1, with a show-calculation view. Unverified.

feature: Sim panel: short-circuit and standards checks
what: Loop impedance Zs, pass/fail text on immediate disconnection (Type C, per electricity law), impedance triangle
home: Earth-fault loop check with earthing system and disconnection time; artboard 4; Phase 1/2
notes: Fixed 0.8 V/Zs vs 10 In rule must go. Needs standards profile
recWhy: Earth-fault loop check is a core result, shown with formula, inputs and clause.

what: Cumulative drop in V and ratio
recWhy: Cumulative voltage drop is one result block with the main results.

feature: Sim panel: UPS / DC UPS management

home: Converter + battery + bypass composition; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Brief: merge or compose UPS
recWhy: UPS status is a composition of converter, battery and bypass, so it follows those in Phase 4.

what: "Waiting for selection" message
recWhy: An empty-state hint in the results panel costs little and orients new users.

what: Log of switching actions with editable notes, add manual row, move up/down, delete row, import log (JSON), export log, clear (with confirm)
home: Switching order recorded from simulation; artboard 4 log and artboard 9; Phase 3
notes: Import errors use alert(); move to problems panel. Log must persist when mode switches
recWhy: Editable switching log feeds the switching order; errors go to the problems panel and the log survives mode changes.

feature: Log footer: generate switching order, load balance report buttons
what: Buttons "Generate switching order (PDF)" and "Load balance report"
recWhy: Both buttons become entries in a documents menu; the load report entry waits for Phase 4.

what: Bottom panel: counts by severity (fault, warning, operational, info), filter checkboxes, export to Excel, clear, per-row zoom-to and remove
home: Problems panel with severity and click-to-select, artboard 1 (Editor) and artboard 4 log; Phase 2
notes: Replaces alert() boxes as well as this feed. Export to spreadsheet is extra and LATER
recWhy: The problems panel with severity, click-to-select and a fix per entry replaces both the alert feed and alert() boxes; spreadsheet export later.

what: Rotate, group into subsystem, ungroup, align and distribute, copy, cut, paste, duplicate, lock/unlock, z-order (front, back, forward, backward), delete
recWhy: Edit commands are relied on; group and ungroup entries only arrive with the Phase 4 visual collapse. Unverified.

notes: Same operations as the toolbox (UI-017)
recWhy: Same feature as ED-050; every action must be a real command, with no Hebrew text built in logic, and it feeds the switching order.

what: A4 preview: order number, work description, location, written date/time, team leader and members, execution date and times, safety equipment checklist with counts, action table, notes, approvals table, return approval; edit fields in place
notes: Header block hard-codes IAF-style document numbers and "edition 18". Neutral editable template needed. Preview file only partly read: unverified
recWhy: Neutral editable template with configurable numbering, steps, lock-out points, voltage-absence check, signatures and optional user logo.

notes: Brief lists "document, PDF" exports. Print popup failure uses alert()
recWhy: Print and PDF are needed for the first release; Word with right-to-left layout is costly, so confirm it is wanted.

what: Hierarchical table of monitored components with planned (design) or measured loads, panels and stations summary, status badges (ok, high, overload, unmeasured), trend charts, reset measurement; export to Excel, Word, print/PDF

notes: Two modes: design report and sim measurement. Phase 3 documents list does not include it
recWhy: Same feature as CH-092; keep with configurable status thresholds and shown formulas, once aggregation exists in Phase 4.

what: Trend line chart (percent and A) and peak bar chart in report; also per-component graph modal
home: Load analysis view; no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: Trend and peak charts need live time-series that the design drops (see SIM-043). Static load tables cover it. Your call.

what: Set earth leakage current (A) per component or wire; meter shows % of trip threshold
home: Fault tools in simulate overlay; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Ties to RCD behaviour; RCD types in design finding
recWhy: Leakage and RCD behaviour belong with the Phase 4 fault tools. Unverified.

home: Design system tokens, themes, 12 px minimum type; artboard 1; Phase 2
notes: Replaces `!important` overrides with tokens
recWhy: Appearance settings (theme, text size, contrast, motion) go to the Phase 2 design system; simulation options stay on the console.

what: Name stamped on every saved file as created/updated by
home: Editions identity adapter; no mockup yet; Phase 6
notes: Brief: OS-username lookup leaked into the app
recWhy: A user name only matters once editions and accounts exist; Phase 2 can leave it out.

notes: Design drops simple/detailed and legacy solver: one calculation. Keep which results to show as view toggles
recWhy: One calculation with view toggles for which results to show; simple/detailed mode and legacy solver are dropped.

what: First-run gate with acknowledgement checkbox, name field, "continue"; reachable later as reference
notes: Text says "aids for practice" and engineer-sign-off; must be rewritten for verified-numbers claim. Not a blocking gate necessarily: owner decision
recWhy: Keep a one-time notice and a reference page, but drop the mandatory name field; a blocking acknowledgement is a legal call.

what: Version history by Added/Fixed etc.
home: Release notes; no mockup yet; Phase 6
notes: Low value early
recWhy: Release notes as a link or page, not a dialog; nobody needs an in-app version history before editions exist.

what: Modal: start tutorial, policy link, navigation, wiring, context menu, keyboard shortcuts, simulation, operational toolbox, changelog
home: First-run checklist plus help, artboard 3; Phase 2
notes: Shortcut list kept as a help reference
recWhy: Help becomes part of the first-run checklist with the shortcut list kept as reference. Unverified.

what: 5 topics, ~25 steps (header, library, hands-on adding, properties, wiring, zones, subsystems, simulation, switching log, PDF order) with spotlight and forced actions
notes: 1,285 lines; steps tied to DOM markers (`data-tutorial`). Replaced by checklist; target is first feeder in under ten minutes
recWhy: A 1,285-line DOM-bound overlay that wipes work is replaced by the non-destructive checklist. Unverified.

what: Generic OK/Cancel confirm
home: Shared dialog primitive; design system; Phase 2
recWhy: Confirm dialog stays for destructive actions only, since browser alert and confirm dialogs are banned.

what: Section card, data row, validated input, combo box (type-to-search with auto option), tooltip
notes: Rebuild on tokens with units, ranges and disabled-reason text
recWhy: Shared controls are design-system components; the type-to-search combo box is worth keeping.

what: Phone layout with bottom bar (Details, Log, Alerts, Fit all) and bottom sheets at peek/half/full
home: Read-only phone view; no mockup yet
notes: Brief keeps the bottom-sheet idea; mobile editing is a non-goal
recWhy: Read-only phone view may come later; mobile editing is a non-goal, so whether to ship it is a product call.

what: Menu: sim settings, open file, save file, theme, accessibility, help, what's new
recWhy: Phone menu belongs with the later read-only phone view; mobile editing is a non-goal.

what: Severity filter chips, export Excel, clear, zoom-to, remove
notes: Phone variant follows later
recWhy: Same problems panel as UI-054; only the phone layout differs and follows later.

what: Toggles between EDIT and SIM; switching to EDIT clears simValues, networkState and simLog.
home: Design "Visible modes" and the Edit/Sim-becomes-one-layout finding; Artboard 1 Editor with Artboard 2 Calculation console; Phase 2
notes: Design says one layout. Many rows below (ED-050 to ED-054, ED-062) exist only because of this split.
recWhy: Edit and simulate share one layout; results overlay the diagram and never clear edit state or the log.

what: Clicks the Header toggle to choose Select or Zone tool (EDIT only).
notes: Only 2 tools exist; no Escape or key shortcut switches tools.
recWhy: Select and zone tools are required; add Escape and key shortcuts per the visible-modes rule. Unverified.

what: Click selects a component, wire or zone; click empty canvas (without Shift) clears selection.
notes: Wire ids are `wire-<id>` strings. Selection ids mix types, and Ctrl+C parses `wire-N` with parseInt, which is fragile. Use typed ids.
recWhy: Click select is essential; use typed ids instead of parsed wire-N strings. Unverified.

what: Shift-click toggles an item; dragging on empty canvas draws a box that selects intersecting components and zones.
notes: Marquee ignores wires and skips hidden or locked zones and other subsystems. Marquee selects on touch of the box edge (intersect, not contain).
recWhy: Shift-click and marquee are standard; include wires in the marquee, which Blue Grid skips. Unverified.

what: Ctrl/Cmd+A: with one component selected inside a zone it selects that zone's contents, else everything in the current subsystem.
notes: Keys: Ctrl/Cmd+A. Two-stage behaviour is hidden and surprising. Hidden or locked zones are excluded (patched).
recWhy: Hidden two-stage Select all is surprising; make Ctrl+A plain and add an explicit select-zone-contents command. Unverified.

what: Drags a component; all selected items move together; a locked primary item will not move.
notes: Wires re-route on mouse-up; during drag they draw straight (fast path). One undo step per drag.
recWhy: Group drag with one undo step per drag is needed; locked items must stay put and snap to grid applies.

what: Components, zones, waypoints and drops snap to 20 px grid when snap is on (default on).
notes: Snap uses the first port as the anchor so ports land on grid lines. Toggle persisted in localStorage (see ED-079).
recWhy: Snap to grid with port-anchored alignment is relied on by electricians. Unverified.

what: Press R or use context menu to rotate selected components 90 degrees clockwise; CCW only via context menu.
notes: Keys: R (CW). Skips locked. Labels counter-rotate to stay upright.
recWhy: R rotates clockwise and skips locked items as in Blue Grid; add counter-clockwise on Shift+R and keep labels upright.

what: Context menu Mirror rotates 180 degrees.
notes: Mirror is just a 180 rotation, not a real flip, so the name is misleading. Decide whether true mirror is needed.
recWhy: Verified: Mirror just adds 180 degrees, which two rotations already give; a true flip is unneeded for single-line symbols.

what: Drags square handles on a selected resizable component (busbar width, rectangle, circle, text, arrow endpoints).
notes: Per-type handleResize in the component definition; fits the registry rule. Busbar width in grid units. Skips locked.
recWhy: Busbar width resize is essential; annotation resize follows the same handles and must respect locks.

what: Arrow keys move selected components and zones one grid step.
notes: Keys: ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight. Skips locked components, but moves locked zones (inconsistent). No Shift for fine or large step.
recWhy: Arrow nudge is useful; apply locks to zones and components alike and add a Shift step. Unverified.

what: Delete or Backspace removes selected items plus attached wires; deleting a non-empty subsystem asks for confirmation.
home: Design "Editor" and the Delete-on-hidden/locked patch; Artboard 1; Phase 2
notes: Keys: Delete, Backspace. RISK: handleDeleteSelected has no locked check, so a locked component can still be deleted, and Ctrl+X ignores locked. Design says it was patched, so add a test. Subsystem delete is recursive.
recWhy: Delete is essential; locked items must be protected from delete and cut, with a test. Unverified.

what: Ctrl/Cmd+C, X, V copy or cut selection with internal wires, and paste at view centre with new ids.
notes: Keys: Ctrl/Cmd+C, Ctrl/Cmd+X, Ctrl/Cmd+V. Clipboard is in memory only (not the OS clipboard, no paste across projects). Cut does not honour locks. Pasted wires keep an original endpoint if the other end was not copied. Pasted wires are not selected. Zone paste may leave nested subsystem contents behind.
recWhy: Copy, cut and paste are expected; honour locks and select pasted items. Unverified.

what: Context menu Duplicate copies selected components offset by one grid step, without wires.
notes: Same as copy+paste; drop as a separate command or keep as a shortcut over paste. Does not copy wires or zones.
recWhy: Duplicate is copy plus paste; keep as a shortcut over paste. Unverified.

what: Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl/Cmd+Y redoes; header buttons do the same.
home: Design "Decision 3: how edits are written and undone" (command log, undo appends a compensating command); Phase 2
notes: Keys: Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Y. Today: snapshot history of whole {components, wires, locations}, depth 50 (MAX_HISTORY), no-change commits skipped by JSON compare, history reset on project load. New model makes depth bounded by the log, not 50. Several edits (property typing, Z-order, align) commit differently from drags; verify per command.
recWhy: Undo appends a compensating command in the log; one user action must equal one undo step, unlike the 50-snapshot history.

what: Drags from a port to another component's port to create a wire; same-component loops are ignored.
home: Design "Nets and compound wires" decision; Artboard 1 and 5 Compound wire; Phase 2
notes: Every new wire gets hidden defaults (N2XY, 150 mm2, 100 m, showLabel) which design flags as a defect; replace with visible unspecified state and a problems-panel entry. Busbar port is chosen by drop x position.
recWhy: Wire drawing creates a compound wire on a net with visible unspecified state, not hidden N2XY 150 mm2 100 m defaults. Unverified.

what: Wire auto-routes around components in orthogonal mode, or draws a straight line in direct mode.
notes: Per-wire routingMode plus a default toggle in CanvasControls (orthogonal or direct; not persisted). A* has a 2000 iteration cap and straight-line fallback; result cache keyed per wire id. Routing belongs in the scene layer, not the model.
recWhy: Orthogonal and direct routing are used daily; keep routing in the scene layer, not the model. Unverified.

what: Selected wire shows handles; drag a waypoint to move it, drag a segment split handle to add one, double-click a waypoint to remove it.
notes: Setting any waypoint turns off auto-routing for that wire and resets pathOffset. Moving or adding waypoints on a locked wire is not checked.
recWhy: Manual waypoints are expected; apply locks to waypoint edits. Unverified.

what: Right-click on a wire gives Select and Delete only.
notes: Delete here removes by array index, not by id. Use ids.
recWhy: Wire context menu stays; act on ids, not array indexes, and add expand-conductors. Unverified.

what: Zone tool: drag a rectangle; tool returns to Select; zone named "Zone".
notes: Min 2 grid units when snapping, else ignored below 20 px. Name is a hard-coded English string. Location names feed getComponentLocation text used in logs.
recWhy: Zones are drawn in Phase 2; localise the default name. Unverified.

what: Drags a zone to move it, or its four corner handles to resize (min 1 grid unit).
notes: Moving a zone does not move contained components. Locked zones hide handles and block moves.
recWhy: Zone move and resize belong with zone drawing. Unverified.

feature: Zone selection pane (hide / lock / rename / zoom)

what: Shows branded loading state
notes: Cosmetic; only list if shell needs it.
recWhy: A plain loading state is needed in the shell; no branding or organisation logo.

feature: Single-click operation of switches in SIM, Ctrl+click select without operating
what: Operates breakers in simulation
recWhy: Click-to-operate is an editor interaction; the operating rules are engine Phase 1, so the click belongs with the Phase 2 editor.

what: Prevents operating a locked device
notes: Visible rule: a locked device refuses all operations and logs the block.

what: Refuses switching that violates interlock

feature: No opening of disconnector under load: ARC fault
what: Opening a disconnector or earth switch under load creates an arc fault and de-energises downstream
notes: Visible rule; must also affect the order generator.
recWhy: Opening a disconnector under load is a core safety rule on a core-eight component; it also needs to feed the order generator.

feature: Earth switch three positions, grounds bottom port only
what: Models earthing correctly
home: Catalog, Phase 1 (core set includes earthing disconnector)
notes: Rule: voltage from the grounded side sees an open circuit.
recWhy: Same feature as COMP-020; earthing disconnector is a core component, so merge into the switch with an earthing capability, keeping the open-circuit rule.

feature: Tripped devices reset only to open; RCD reset by click
what: Enforces reset rule
recWhy: Trip resets only to open is a core breaker rule; the RCD click-reset part follows with the RCD in Phase 4.

what: Tells the user why an action was refused
notes: Replace alert boxes with explained reasons.
recWhy: The shake is dropped (ED-087); the refusal message already comes from the problems panel (CH-096), so this row adds nothing.

feature: Operational toolbox (LOTO, portable earthing, artificial fault, fuse replace, leakage, monitor)
what: Applies operator tools by drag or right-click
recWhy: Operator tools (lock-out, portable earth, artificial fault) are real work practice and feed the switching order; the toolbox UI lands with the documents phase.

feature: Switching log (timeline, status pills, standardized Hebrew action text, zone attribution, manual rows, notes, import/export, clear)
what: Records every operation for the switching order
home: Views and documents (switching order), artboard 9, Phase 3
notes: Log text via message catalogs, not Hebrew strings in logic.
recWhy: Log texts come from message catalogs, not Hebrew strings in logic; it feeds the Phase 3 switching order.

feature: Switching order document (PDF/print, Word RTL, repeating header, page numbers, signature block, order number)
what: Produces the formal switching order
notes: Owner decision 13: neutral, configurable template; no IAF logos.
recWhy: Neutral configurable template with repeating header, page numbers and signature block; part of the first release.

feature: Switching order from a rehearsed simulation sequence
what: Compiles simulated actions into numbered checklist
recWhy: Switching order generation is a first-release document; merged into CH-051.

feature: Load flow: voltages, currents, power (P, Q, S), power factor display
what: Shows live network values
notes: Re-derive against references.
recWhy: Load flow with P, Q, S and power factor is in the first calculation gate and must be re-derived with traces.

feature: Voltage drop (local, cumulative, % vs local nominal)
what: Shows drop along the path
recWhy: Voltage drop is in the Phase 1 gate; it needs local and cumulative values with the profile limit.

what: Shows loss from source to any point
recWhy: Cumulative losses follow directly from the same solve and belong with the Phase 1 load flow.

feature: Per-phase (L1/L2/L3) monitoring of voltage, angle, current
what: Shows per-phase values on 3-phase nodes
home: Engine ("Unbalanced loads on a balanced solver"), artboard 4, Phase 1
notes: Flow Engine labels these "balanced-model estimate".
recWhy: Per-phase values on a balanced solver are acceptable if labelled as a balanced-model estimate, as the design states.

what: Graphical display of impedance and power
notes: Optional visual on the trace.
recWhy: Impedance and power triangles are an optional teaching visual on the trace; Phase 2 is already full with the editor.

feature: Impedance-aware load sharing on meshes and parallel paths (admittance)
what: Splits current among parallel paths
notes: Net-based nodal solve replaces it.
recWhy: Parallel-path current sharing comes naturally from the net-based nodal solve, so it needs no separate feature.

feature: Iterative power-flow, mesh (Gauss-Seidel) solver, solver selector
what: Converged load flow for radial and meshed networks
notes: Flow Engine has no legacy fallback or user selector.
recWhy: One iterative mesh solver in Phase 1 with no legacy fallback and no user-selectable solver.

what: Picks a quick or full calculation
notes: Rejected: user cannot tell which numbers they see.
recWhy: One calculation only; users cannot tell which numbers they are seeing in a simplified mode.

feature: Reactive power and impedance chain (R/X, transformer %Z, source MVA)
what: Models real impedances
notes: Concept brief flags the transformer side error.
recWhy: Impedance chain must be rebuilt with a known-answer 22 kV/0.4 kV test, since the transformer side error is unproven either way.

feature: IEC 60909 style fault currents (Ik max, Ik min, c factors, temperature correction)
what: Computes fault currents at every node
notes: Full sequence networks and all sources.
recWhy: Blue Grid uses one shortest path and fixed X/R; Flow Engine needs sequence networks with all sources, as the design says.

feature: Earth-loop impedance Zs and Israeli protection check
what: Verifies disconnection on earth fault
home: Engine ("Cable sizing and earth-fault loop"), Phase 1
notes: Adds earthing system and disconnection time.
recWhy: Earth-fault loop with disconnection time is in the Phase 1 gate and is under the standards profile.

feature: Protection trip logic (overcurrent, fuse blow, over/under-voltage, source overload)
what: Trips devices above thresholds
notes: Time-current curves and selectivity; enable-protection flag becomes visible setting.
recWhy: Instant breaker trip, voltage limits and source overload are Phase 1 (SIM-012, 015, 016); only curves and selectivity wait for Phase 4.

what: Turns protection on or off
notes: Unverified exact flag name.
recWhy: Protection on or off must be an explicit visible setting shown with results, not a hidden flag.

feature: Faults on cables generate short-circuit current
what: Models cable faults
recWhy: Cable-fault current in Blue Grid falls back to ik_max or a silent 1000 A default; it must come from the short-circuit calculation.

what: Models adjustable trip unit
notes: Brief: a protection profile, not a separate type.
recWhy: Owner says electronic breaker becomes a protection profile on the switch, not a separate type; keep L/S/I/G settings in the profile.

feature: Trip delay and "impending trip" countdown with trip time shown
what: Shows time to trip and actual trip time
recWhy: Impending-trip countdown depends on time-current curves, which arrive in Phase 4.

feature: TCC curve viewer (log-log, L S I G) with PNG save
what: Plots the protection curve
notes: Chart must be derived from catalog device data.
recWhy: Curve viewer must be drawn from catalog device data with the protection and selectivity work.

feature: RCD: leakage threshold, trip at >=, power cut when open or tripped
what: Models residual-current protection
notes: Needs RCD types per concept brief.
recWhy: Same feature as COMP-023; RCD is not in the core eight and needs earth-fault logic, so one consistent Phase 4 entry.

feature: Leakage tool, leakage editor, purple indicator, cumulative leakage, header alert, gauge
what: Sets and shows earth-leakage current
recWhy: Leakage must sum upstream so an upstream RCD trips; Blue Grid reads only the component's own leakage (Protection.ts, LoadFlow.ts).

what: Re-solves only what changed
notes: Port expected numbers, rewrite.
recWhy: One solver per power island is the design; port expected numbers, not code or the signature cache.

feature: Engine in a Web Worker with fallback
what: Keeps the UI responsive
notes: Concept brief: keep the coalescing protocol.
recWhy: Worker keeps the UI responsive and the coalescing protocol is sound; build it in the Phase 1 engine.

feature: Spatial culling and zoom-dependent detail levels
what: Scales to 1,000+ components
notes: SVG then canvas hand-over.
recWhy: Same feature as ED-044; keep the spatial index and detail levels but redo them for the SVG then canvas rendering.

what: Feeds single-phase loads from a 3-phase network
home: Project model (compound wire splits to conductors), artboard 5, Phase 2
notes: Disappears if wires split into conductors.
recWhy: The phase splitter disappears once wires split into conductors; single-phase loads connect to one conductor.

feature: Mixed AC 3-ph, AC 1-ph, DC with colours (DC blue)
what: Supports several power types
notes: Color roles redefined; red reserved for alarms.
recWhy: Power types drive separate solvers; colours are redefined with red kept for alarms.

feature: Converters: inverter, rectifier, DC/DC, VFD, efficiency
what: Converts between power types
notes: Efficiency percent vs decimal rule fixed in v0.21.3.
recWhy: Owner merges inverter, rectifier, DC-DC and VFD into one converter; Phase 4 with DC support is right.

feature: Input and output power/current shown separately for converters and transformers
what: Shows losses at conversion
recWhy: Showing input and output power across transformers and converters exposes losses and is cheap once solved.

feature: Transformer (ratio, vector group, %Z, losses, phase shift)
what: Models transformers
notes: Core set; impedance side verified by test.
recWhy: Transformer is core; ratio, vector group and impedance side need real reference cases instead of regex parsing.

what: Sets source strength
recWhy: Grid is core; replace the 999999 MVA student default with an explicit entered short-circuit level.

what: Models gensets
recWhy: Generator is core (COMP-002 says Phase 1); only fuel and synchronising logic wait for Phase 4.

feature: Fuel simulation toggle, fuel tank, shutdown when empty
what: Models fuel use
notes: String link replaced by ID link.
recWhy: Fuel simulation is not core; keep as Phase 4 with an ID link replacing the string link.

what: Parallel-connects sources
recWhy: Synchroniser folds into the control-logic layer after the core eight work.

feature: ATS, ATS controller (state machine, delays, sequences)
what: Automatic transfer
notes: Brief: one logic layer; two components do same job.
recWhy: ATS and its controller duplicate each other and become one control-logic feature.

feature: UPS and DC UPS (state machine, battery, bypass, backup time, sidebar panel)
what: Models UPS operation
recWhy: Same as COMP-010/011: UPS is a template over converter, battery and bypass, keeping the mode behaviour electricians rely on.

feature: Battery bank (SOC, charge, time remaining), PV array, EV charger toggle
what: Models storage, PV, EV
notes: Not in the core set.
recWhy: Battery, PV and EV are not core; align with COMP-003/004 as Phase 4, and EV charger merges into load.

feature: Current stabilizer (CCR): input type, two-output option, efficiency, open-circuit TRIP
what: Models constant-current regulator
notes: Power type, not component quirk.
recWhy: CCR is a series-loop power type with compliance voltage and real open-circuit detection, not a component quirk.

feature: Light, horn, current load as constant-impedance loads
what: Series-loop loads
recWhy: Light, horn and current load merge into the single load; constant-impedance behaviour matters for series loops in Phase 4.

what: Models fuses
recWhy: Fuse is not in the core eight and its curve belongs with protection and selectivity in Phase 4; match COMP-022.

feature: Busbar (variable width/ports), combiner box, pole, SPD, connector (wireless address)
what: Structure and node components
home: Topology and the busbar rule, Phase 1
notes: Combiner merges into DC busbar; SPD and pole dropped as simulated parts.
recWhy: Busbar and connector are modelled in the Phase 1 topology; combiner becomes a DC busbar and SPD and pole are dropped. Unverified.

feature: Load-balance module: monitored components, time-weighted avg/max, diversity factors
what: Measures and reports loading
home: Engine ("Simplification" load aggregation), no mockup yet, Phase 4

recWhy: Static load aggregation with diversity factors is the design's view over the full calculation; live monitoring is not carried over.

feature: Load-balance report (hierarchy, reserve, imbalance, status, panel summary; print/Word/Excel)

home: Views and documents, no mockup yet, Phase 4
recWhy: Report carries hierarchy, planned versus simulated, reserve, per-phase imbalance and shown formulas; needs Phase 4 aggregation.

what: Plans load from nameplates
recWhy: Design-mode load report is the same feature as the load aggregation view.

feature: Monitoring badge, live load meters, 80% / 100% load alerts
what: Flags overloaded feeders
recWhy: Keep the 80% and 100% loading warnings as advice rules in the problems panel; drop the live meters and monitoring badge.

what: Shows per-component load history
recWhy: Per-component load history needs the dropped time-series monitoring (see SIM-043). Your call.

feature: System alerts log (toast, severity filters, locate, remove, Excel export)

notes: Replaces alert boxes.
recWhy: The problems panel replaces Blue Grid's alert log; severity filter and locate stay, Excel export is optional.

what: Jumps to the offending element
notes: Click selects element.
recWhy: Click-to-select and zoom to the offending element is part of the problems panel.

recWhy: Electricians read currents in 3x100A notation; tooltip should also link to the calculation trace.

feature: Animated power flow on wires with phase colour
what: Visualises energisation
notes: Colour families changed.
recWhy: Same feature as ED-080, which defers animation to Phase 4; static energised colouring comes with results display. Unverified.

feature: SIM sidebar sections (collapsible, hero status card, UPS/battery/fuel/sync widgets)
what: Shows details of the selected item
recWhy: Results detail moves into the one persistent layout and trace view; separate Simulate sidebar widgets are not carried over.

feature: Calculation display toggles (show current, voltage, power)
what: Chooses what values appear
recWhy: Choosing visible values is useful; the toggles must not hide numbers a trace needs.

what: Views and simulates on a phone
decisionText: LATER (read-only phone view, no phase named)
notes: Concept brief: mobile editing out of scope; read-only phone view may follow. Keep bottom-sheet idea.
recWhy: Read-only phone viewing later; the simulate controls and bottom action bar are not carried over.

feature: Touch gestures (pan, pinch, long-press) and discard of leftover tap after gesture
what: Safe touch operation
notes: Rule: never operate a breaker from a gesture's trailing click.
recWhy: Touch is later and read-only; keep the rule that a trailing click after a gesture never operates a breaker.

feature: Electron desktop app, portable EXE, single-instance lock
what: Runs as standalone app
notes: Optional Electron wrapper.
recWhy: Electron is optional and later; the single-instance lock is a platform detail.

what: Runs offline with no server
notes: Offline-capable web app for LTS edition.
recWhy: Offline use comes with the long-term-support edition as an installable web app; a single-file build is a distribution choice.

feature: Automated test suite and Playwright e2e
what: Guards behaviour
notes: Reference cases from outside the code.
recWhy: Tests and CI rules are a Phase 0 requirement; Playwright e2e grows with the editor in Phase 2.

what: Independent review of physics changes
notes: Stale; concept brief says the tests prove self-consistency only.
recWhy: A review process document, not an app feature; verification lives in the reference cases.

home: Catalog and standards layer; Editor 1, Results 4; Phase 1 (core)
notes: Short-circuit MVA default "infinite" is flagged in-code as a student default. Triage says redesign string links, not this one.
recWhy: Grid is a core component; default must be an entered value, not an infinite bus.

what: Local source (1000 kVA, 12% Z) that cannot be started with an empty tank when fuel simulation is on and a tank link exists.
home: Catalog; Editor 1; Phase 1 (core); fuel and sync logic Phase 4
notes: Fuel link is a loose string id (`fuelTankId`). Duplicated validateAction inline in the definition and in the registry.
recWhy: Generator is core; fuel and sync logic follow in Phase 4 and the duplicated validate logic is not carried over.

what: DC source (800 V, 50 kWp) with simple on/off toggle.
notes: Triage says KEEP; not in the eight core components. No irradiance or MPPT behaviour seen.
recWhy: PV array is outside the core set and needs DC support; Phase 4 is right.

what: DC source/sink with SoC; reads as charging when external voltage is at or above charging voltage, and is dead at 0% SoC.
notes: Triage KEEP. SoC integrated from flowP in useSimulation.
recWhy: Battery bank needs DC and charge state; Phase 4, and the UPS should reuse it instead of a hidden battery.

what: Steps voltage by ratio, shifts phase by vector-group clock number x 30 degrees, applies %Z, no-load and copper losses; blocks DC.
home: Catalog and standards layer; Editor 1, Results 4; Phase 1 (core)
notes: Vector group is regex-parsed from a string (`/\d+$/`). Solver assumes fixed 0.98 efficiency in load flow (engineeringConstants) while physics has losses: two models.
recWhy: Transformer is core; redesign removes the regex vector group and the fixed 0.98 efficiency, using IEC 60909 impedance correction.

what: DC to AC converter with set output voltage and efficiency; requires DC input.
notes: Synchronizer can nudge its V/f/phase (treated as a source).
recWhy: Owner merges inverter into one converter; Phase 4.

what: AC to DC converter using 1.35 x Vac (3-phase) or 0.9 x Vac (1-phase).
notes: Fixed factors, no ripple or load dependence.
recWhy: Owner merges rectifier into one converter; fixed 1.35 and 0.9 factors become a stated assumption.

what: DC to DC converter forcing the set output voltage.
notes: Default 48 V in, 400 V out.
recWhy: Owner merges DC-DC into one converter; Phase 4.

what: Active converter forcing output frequency and voltage, passing phase through.
notes: Impedance fixed 0.01.
recWhy: Owner merges VFD into one converter; frequency control becomes a converter mode.

what: AC UPS with OFF / BYPASS / BATTERY / ONLINE modes, backup minutes and recharge factor.
notes: Hidden internal battery duplicates BATTERY_BANK, per triage.
recWhy: UPS becomes converter plus battery plus bypass; removes the hidden duplicate battery.

what: AC to DC supply with internal battery backup.
notes: Same duplicate-battery issue.
recWhy: DC UPS is the same composition with a DC output, so it merges with the UPS template.

what: General consumer by kVA, load percentage, power factor, optional leakage and operational/administrative flag.
decisionText: KEEP (becomes the single load with a mode)
notes: Target of MERGE for COMP-013..015.
recWhy: Load is core and becomes the single load with kVA, amps and operational-flag modes.

what: Consumer specified by current in amps instead of kVA.
notes: Not even counted as a load in LoadFlow (only LOAD, EV_CHARGER, LIGHT, HORN get power). Possibly dead behaviour.
recWhy: Owner merges current load into load; loadBalance.ts does read its target current, so keep the amps mode.

what: Lighting consumer (0.1 kVA, PF 0.9).
notes: Series loop use is a CUJ 6 / Phase 4 matter.
recWhy: Owner merges light into load as a symbol; only series-loop use needs Phase 4 behaviour.

what: Alarm horn consumer (0.05 kVA, PF 0.8).
notes: Not a real behaviour difference.
recWhy: Owner merges horn into load as a symbol; no real behaviour difference.

what: Switchable station (AC or DC, 22 kW) that only energizes if input type matches.
notes: Triage KEEP and redesign. Power divides by PF in LoadFlow.
recWhy: A switchable AC or DC consumer is a load with a type match; merge into load rather than keeping a fourth consumer type.

what: Breaker that can break load, with states open/closed/trip; reset goes trip to open.
home: Catalog; Editor 1, Results 4, Switching order 9; Phase 1 (core)
notes: Overcurrent trip is instant over currentRating, no curve.
recWhy: Owner merges breaker into one switch with a capability set; breaker is core, so Phase 1.

what: Load-break switch, same physics as breaker, no short-circuit protection.
notes: Registry gives it plain toggle only.
recWhy: Load-break switch is a switch with load-break but no short-circuit capability; owner merges it.

what: Isolator that cannot be opened under load; opening when current above 0.1 A is blocked and creates an arc fault.
notes: The arc then sets `isFaulted` permanently on the device (App.tsx). Current uses sqrt(3) for all types, wrong for DC and 1-phase.
recWhy: Merge into switch; keep the no-open-under-load rule but drop the permanent isFaulted arc hack and per-type sqrt(3) use.

what: Three-position device (closed, open, grounded) cycled by click; grounded state shorts to earth.
notes: Grounded does not fault if power enters port 0 (VoltagePropagation). Cycle logic lives in switchingLogic, not the definition.
recWhy: Earthing disconnector is core; merge as a switch with earthing capability, keeping the open-circuit rule from the earthed side.

what: Breaker with LSIG settings (L, S, I, G, pickup and delays) and countdown warning before trip.
decisionText: REDESIGN (as protection profile on the switch)
home: Engine, protection and selectivity; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Triage: keep as profile.
recWhy: Becomes a protection profile on the switch, with LSIG curves arriving with protection and selectivity.

what: Overcurrent fuse that blows (opens permanently) above rating and cannot be toggled while blown.
notes: Replace needs a service action. Blow requires trips-enabled setting.
recWhy: Fuse stays as its own type with a time-current curve, which fits Phase 4 protection work.

what: Residual-current device tripping when leakage reaches threshold (default 30 mA).
notes: Leakage is read only from the RCD node's own property; not summed from downstream (see SIM-014).
recWhy: RCD stays; leakage must be summed from downstream, so it needs the Phase 4 earth-fault logic.

what: Variable-width node with a user-set port count, for joining circuits.
home: Topology and the busbar rule; Editor 1; Phase 1
notes: Port count is a user property, per triage. In Flow Engine it becomes a net plus a rating rule.
recWhy: Busbar is core and becomes a net with a rating rule instead of a user-set port count.

what: DC box with 3 inputs and one output.
home: Topology and the busbar rule; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: No physics in registry, only a pass-through node.
recWhy: Owner merges combiner box into a DC busbar; it has no physics of its own.

what: Splits a 3-phase feed into three single-phase legs at 0 / -120 / +120 degrees.
home: Project model (compound wire split); Editor 1, Compound wire 5; Phase 2
notes: Disappears when a wire can split into conductors. Reverse flow flagged as error.
recWhy: Owner says phase splitter disappears once wires split into conductors; compound wire (Phase 2) replaces it.

what: Constant-current regulator (default 6.6 A) with one or two outputs that forces series current on downstream loads.
home: Engine (series constant-current loop); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: The "open circuit TRIP" error that triggers its trip is checked in Protection but nothing in simulation/ sets it. Possibly dead path.
recWhy: Constant-current regulator becomes a series-loop source; the dead open-circuit trip path is not carried over.

what: Logic block that pulls linked generators or inverters to the master's V/f/phase and releases linked interlocks when synced.
home: Engine, switching logic; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Wired by string id list `targets`.
recWhy: Folds into the single control-logic layer, with node references instead of string id lists.

what: Logic block with XOR or AND rule over a target list that blocks switching.
home: Engine, switching logic; Switching order 9; Phase 1 for the check, Phase 4 for authoring
notes: The brief says the XOR setting is stored and never used; in this code `logicType` is read in switchingLogic.ts, so that brief claim looks wrong.
recWhy: Interlocks must exist when the switching order ships (Phase 3); XOR is read in switchingLogic.ts, so the brief's claim is wrong.

what: Logic block that runs automatic mains/backup/generator changeover with delay and cooldown timers.
notes: Duplicates ATS. Heuristic uses `ofType('GRID')[0]` for mains availability.
recWhy: Merges with ATS into one control-logic feature; mains availability must not be 'first grid is on'.

what: Two-position (main/backup) transfer switch with its own delay and cooldown properties.

recWhy: Merge into the control-logic layer; delay and cooldown properties were unused by the engine.

what: Wireless goto/from node: all connectors with the same address are electrically joined.
home: Topology and the busbar rule; Editor 1; Phase 2
notes: Defined twice (Connector.tsx and Nodes.tsx); subsystem ports match connectors by label text.
recWhy: Off-page connector stays as a net label bound by ID, not by label text; fits the net-based model.

what: Surge protection device drawn as a symbol; no registry physics.
notes: Not simulated.
recWhy: Owner drops SPD as a simulated part; it has no physics in Blue Grid.

what: Overhead-line pole with selectable ports; type computed from ports.
home: Editor behaviour; no mockup yet; Phase 2
notes: No physics seen.
recWhy: Owner drops pole; no physics, and a waypoint on a wire covers any drawing need.

what: Diesel tank holding fuel level that generators draw down.
notes: No ports; link to generator is a loose id.
recWhy: Fuel tank is only needed with generator fuel simulation; Phase 4 with an ID link.

what: Container whose mapped ports connect to inner connectors by label; double-click to enter.
home: Views and documents (visual collapse); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Virtual wires built from label match; missing inner connector yields a port-integrity error.
recWhy: Owner wants visual collapse as a view over the full calculation, not a model-rewriting container; Phase 4.

what: Plain rectangle shape.
notes: Outside the electrical model, per triage.
recWhy: Annotation shapes sit outside the electrical model and are needed once the editor exists.

what: Plain circle shape.
notes: Same.
recWhy: Annotation layer shape, per owner decision; Phase 2 editor.

what: Free text box.
notes: Same.
recWhy: Annotation text is needed in the editor; it stays outside the electrical model.

what: Plain arrow.
notes: Same.
recWhy: Annotation arrow, per owner decision; Phase 2 editor.

what: Voltage, phase, frequency and type spread from each energised source through closed switches, accumulating wire and component impedance.
home: Engine and topology (nets); Calculation console 2, Results 4; Phase 1
notes: "First wire wins" and node-per-component graph are the root problem in the brief.
recWhy: Replace first-wire-wins BFS with net derivation and one solver per island.

what: Grid on unless off, generator and PV only when on, battery with SoC above 0, UPS only in BATTERY status.
notes: Battery/UPS parts land in Phase 4.
recWhy: Source gating by state is correct; grid and generator are core, battery and UPS follow in Phase 4.

feature: Open, tripped, blown and grounded devices stop propagation
what: Open or tripped breaker/RCD/CCR, blown fuse and grounded earth switch do not pass power.
notes: Core components only in Phase 1.
recWhy: Open, tripped, blown or grounded devices stopping power is basic behaviour for the core switch types.

what: Two sources meeting out of tolerance (10% or 10 V, 15 degrees, 0.5 Hz, or type mismatch) mark a "short" error naming both sources.
notes: Tolerances are constants to port with the reference tests.
recWhy: Source collision check is needed with grid plus generator; tolerances should be profile settings with a cited basis, not bare constants.

what: Nodes downstream of a faulted parent are de-energised.
recWhy: De-energising downstream of a faulted or open element is expected and falls out of net connectivity.

what: Network is split into islands by union-find and solved separately with per-island signatures to skip unchanged ones.
home: Engine (one solver per power island); Calculation console 2; Phase 1
notes: Brief: port expected numbers, not code.
recWhy: Island decomposition is the design's solver structure; port expected numbers, rewrite the code.

what: Apparent, real and per-phase power of loads roll up to parents, split by admittance across multiple parents, divided by converter or transformer efficiency.
notes: Uses fixed 0.98 transformer efficiency.
recWhy: Roll-up needs real per-device efficiency, not the fixed 0.98; the aggregation view is Phase 4.

what: Single-phase loads attributed to phase 1 by default; phase-splitter outputs map to R/S/T.
notes: Design already labels this an estimate.
recWhy: Phase attribution becomes explicit through conductors instead of defaulting to phase 1; keep the estimate label.

what: Optional cumulative drop along wires from I x Z (sqrt(3) or 2 factor) when drop or loss display is on.
recWhy: Voltage drop must be re-derived with traces and no silent cable defaults, not kept as the Blue Grid code.

what: Optional Ik_max (c=1.1), Ik_min phase-neutral and phase-earth (c=0.95, temperature-corrected R) and loop impedance Zs per node.
home: Engine (short circuit, earth-fault loop); Results 4; Phase 1 or 4 (unverified which)
notes: Source X/R fixed at 10, component at 5.
recWhy: Blue Grid uses one shortest path, fixed X/R of 10 and 5, and a doubted transformer impedance; it needs full IEC 60909 in Phase 1.

what: Right-click fault or portable shorts inject fault load at the live node and raise "short" error; breakers then see overcurrent.
home: Engine and simulation actions; Results 4; Phase 1
notes: Wire fault current uses ik_max or default 1000 A.
recWhy: Applied faults are useful for training; the fault current must come from the calculation, not a 1000 A default.

what: With the trips setting on, a breaker over rating gets a trip intent and goes to "trip" with reason text.
notes: Instant, no curve; curves are Phase 4.
recWhy: Instant overcurrent trip on the core breaker is Phase 1; curves follow later.

what: With trips on, a fuse over rating opens and stays blown until replaced via a service action.
recWhy: Fuse is outside the core eight; keep blow and replace-to-restore behaviour when the type arrives.

what: RCD trips when its node's `leakage` reaches the threshold; leakage is set via a leakage modal on a load or wire.
notes: Reading shows leakage is NOT summed upstream and wire leakageCurrent is not read by the engine, so an RCD upstream of a leaking load would not trip. Verify by test.
recWhy: Confirmed gap: leakage is not summed upstream, so an RCD upstream of a leaking load never trips; fix in redesign.

what: Over- or under-voltage errors against rated voltage with configurable thresholds (defaults 1.1 and 0.9).
recWhy: Over- and under-voltage limits are in the first gate, with thresholds from the standards profile.

what: GEN, GRID and PV error when flowS exceeds capacity.
recWhy: Source overload against capacity is an expected diagnostic on grid and generator.

what: Tripped breaker, RCD and blown fuse show error text with trip data and are de-energised.
recWhy: Tripped devices must be shown as de-energised with the trip cause as a diagnostic code.

what: CCR enters "trip" state when its error equals an open-circuit string.
home: Engine (series loop); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Nothing in simulation/ sets that error string, so trigger appears dead. Design wants compliance voltage and open-circuit detection.
recWhy: Trigger string is set nowhere in simulation/ (Protection.ts:55), so it is dead code; open-circuit detection is covered by SIM-019 and CH-087.

what: Downstream of a CCR, loads are forced to the CCR current and solved as fixed-current branches.
home: Engine (series loop); no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: Series constant-current loop is a Phase 4 power type with its own solver.

what: Backward/forward sweep for radial, Gauss-Seidel nodal for meshes, multi-level meshes via transformers, warm starts; converter-coupled mixes fall back to legacy.
home: Engine (one solver per power island, no legacy fallback); Calculation console 2; Phase 1
notes: Design rejects porting and rejects the legacy fallback.
recWhy: One solver per power island with no legacy fallback; unsolvable cases produce a visible diagnostic.

feature: Solver choice, cadence and worker settings
what: Settings: solver iterative or legacy, cadence balanced (250 ms trailing edge) or realtime, worker on/off, profiling.
notes: Legacy option dropped. Settings stored in browser localStorage.
recWhy: Drop the legacy solver option; keep worker protocol and cadence, with settings visible.

what: One solve in flight, latest args win, stale results dropped.
notes: Brief lists this as an idea worth carrying.
recWhy: One solve in flight with latest-wins coalescing is a sound protocol worth carrying.

what: Toggles for current, power, voltage, drop, losses, overcurrent trips, fault current, fuel simulation; simplified vs detailed mode.
notes: Simplified mode also filters "overcurrent" alerts by message text (useSystemAlerts).
recWhy: Display toggles stay as view options, but filtering alerts by message text must not carry over.

what: Click toggles a device; a trip can only be reset to open; generator and grid toggle on/off.
home: Engine (switching logic); Editor 1, Switching order 9; Phase 1
recWhy: Toggle rules and trip-resets-only-to-open are core switch behaviour electricians rely on.

what: A component marked locked cannot be switched and the block is logged.
notes: Wire lock flag is set in the UI; no wire-lock check found in the engine.
recWhy: Lock-out is a real feature; enforce it for wires too, since the wire lock flag is set but unchecked in the engine.

what: Active interlocks block closing (XOR) or any switching unless all others are closed (AND).
notes: Part of the single control-logic layer.
recWhy: Interlock check is needed once the switching order is generated; the core eight need none in Phase 1.

feature: Arc on opening a disconnector under load
what: Blocked with "opening under load" message and the device becomes faulted.
notes: Fault latches with no repair path seen in the files read.
recWhy: Opening a disconnector under load must block and fault; add an explicit repair or reset path, since the fault latches.

what: Click cycles closed, open, grounded, with direction reversal at the ends.
recWhy: Closed, open, grounded cycle is the earthing disconnector's behaviour and it is a core-eight component.

what: Every switch, LOTO, ground and fuse action is logged with time and location; the log is printed as a maintenance instruction sheet.
home: Views and documents (switching order); Switching order 9; Phase 3
notes: Order is a record of a live rehearsal, not generated from rules; no generation rules found in code.
recWhy: Order is generated from rules by a neutral template, with the live action log kept as a separate record.

what: Nudges linked generators or inverters toward the master V/f/phase (steps 0.5% V, 0.05 Hz, 2 degrees), reports progress and "synced" within 2%, 0.1 Hz, 3 degrees.
home: Engine (control logic); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Weighted progress: phase 60%, frequency 20%, voltage 20%.
recWhy: Synchroniser belongs to the control-logic layer after the core components.

feature: Sync releases interlock and closes switches
what: When synced, the interlock turns off and breakers/switches under it close; stopping sync re-arms it and opens them.
home: Engine (control logic); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Only BREAKER, DISCONNECTOR, LOAD_BREAKER auto-operate.
recWhy: Sync release of interlock and auto-close is control logic, done with the layer in Phase 4.

what: Unsynchronised running generators and inverters drift back to base V/f/phase slowly.
notes: Gives realistic out-of-sync after stop.
recWhy: Drifting generator voltage and frequency is animation realism, not engineering output; a static calculation tool does not need it.

what: Tank level falls by kW x specific consumption (default 0.25 L/kWh); at zero the generator shuts off with an alert.
notes: Only when fuel simulation setting is on and a tank link exists.
recWhy: Fuel runtime is useful for generator sizing; keep as an optional later view tied to a tank link.

what: State machine idle, main_ok, loss_delay, switching_backup, backup_active, return_delay, switching_main; opens main, starts generator, closes backup, then reverses after cooldown.
home: Engine (control logic); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Mains availability is "first GRID is on" only.
recWhy: ATS sequence is control logic; the mains-availability test must not be 'first grid is on'.

what: Status OFF / BYPASS / CHARGING / ONLINE / BATTERY; battery drains by backup time scaled by load ratio (min 10%) and recharges at drain / recharge factor.
notes: Bypass is a user property toggled from the sim panel.
recWhy: UPS states and battery runtime come with the Phase 4 component set.

what: SoC changes by Ah from flowP and nominal voltage; empty battery stops being a source.
recWhy: Battery state-of-charge integration follows the battery component in Phase 4.

what: I instantaneous, S short-time, L inverse-time (t = tr x (6 / (I/Ir))^2, 5% pickup), G ground-fault; countdown warning, trip when timer elapses; plain overcurrent if LSIG off.
home: Engine (protection curves); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Timer counts at 100 ms ticks, so very short delays are tick-quantised. G uses `leakage`, subject to SIM-014 limit.
recWhy: LSIG curves belong with protection profiles; the inverse-time formula and 5% pickup need checking against the standard.

what: Trip intents become state changes, a 500 ms shake and an alert entry.
notes: Engine returns intents; the UI applies them.
recWhy: Engine returns trip intents and the UI applies them; shake animation is a UI choice.

what: Severity critical, warning, info, operational; condition-based alerts fire once per condition and are capped at 50.
home: Engine diagnostics (codes plus parameters), Results 4; Phase 1
notes: Alert text is built in Hebrew in the hook; design wants codes at the engine edge.
recWhy: Diagnostics carry codes and parameters so Hebrew and English text is built at the UI edge.

what: Error alert on any node error; warning at over 100% of capacity or current rating.
recWhy: Node errors and overload warnings at over 100% are core diagnostics in the problems panel.

what: Monitored components alert at over 80% (warning) and over 100% (critical) of their load basis.
home: Views and documents (load aggregation); no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: Loading-percentage alerts come with the load aggregation view; basic overload is already in SIM-040.

what: Warning on battery mode, critical on empty battery, operational on loss of feed to loads (operational vs administrative) and UPS input.
home: Engine diagnostics; no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Load operational flag is user-set.
recWhy: UPS and loss-of-feed alerts follow the UPS and load-criticality features.

what: Time-weighted average and peak of amps, kW and percent for monitored components, energised time only, sampled at 100 ms, committed at 1 Hz, reset on entering sim.
home: Views and documents (load aggregation); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Never persisted.
recWhy: Time-weighted sampling of a live rehearsal does not fit a static calculation; load aggregation covers design loading.

what: One point per second per monitored component, ring buffer of 3600 points (one hour).
home: Views and documents; no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: A one-hour ring buffer of rehearsal samples has no basis in the static calculation model and is never persisted.

what: 100% is Ir for calibrated electronic breaker, In if a rating exists, derived from kVA for capacity types and loads, else none.
home: Engine (load aggregation); no mockup yet; Phase 4
recWhy: A defined load basis (Ir, In, or kVA) is needed for loading percentages and aggregation.

what: Hierarchy built from topology with manual parent override and cycle guard, children peak sum with diversity factor, reserve, phase imbalance, planned kW in edit mode.
home: Views and documents (load aggregation); Circuit schedule 6 related; Phase 4
notes: Report component itself only listed, not read.
recWhy: Load-balance report with diversity and phase imbalance is the aggregation view in Phase 4; unverified report component.

feature: Subsystem virtual wires and port check
what: Subsystem ports map to inner connectors by label; a missing inner connector gives a port-not-connected error.
home: Views and documents (visual collapse); no mockup yet; Phase 4
notes: Label-based match is fragile.
recWhy: Label-matched ports are fragile; the visual collapse should bind ports by node reference.
